clue.text: Plunder overrun by vermin — a source of infection

indicators.note: to be overrun by something is to have it all around you, so the plunder word sits inside the vermin word

parts.note: mice are household vermin
to plunder is to rob

explanation.surface: Rats and mice swarm over stolen goods, spreading disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overrun by' puts ROB inside MICE, splitting it as MIC-ROB-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ or bacterium is a tiny organism that can carry and spread disease.

clue.text: Frenchman is found in the wrong role

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman
taken as written
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: A Frenchman discovered playing a part that does not suit him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like 'discovered' but is the verb of foundry work: to cast metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor given a part they are unsuited to has been badly chosen for it.

clue.text: Vicar touring cam, perhaps, and Chichester

indicators.note: perhaps signals that vicar touring cam may be an arrangement of other letters

explanation.surface: A vicar taking a trip along the Cam is compared with Chichester.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Chichester was the British yachtsman who sailed solo round the world in 1966-67. 'perhaps' rearranges all fifteen letters of 'Vicar touring cam'; the Cam is the river at Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis sailed single-handed around the globe, so he is a famous round-the-world voyager.

clue.text: Obvious case of English king who will do too much

indicators.note: a case holds something inside it, so the obvious word encloses the king and English

parts.note: overt means open and obvious
rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king plainly given to overdoing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' puts REX and E inside OVERT: OVE-REXE-RT. 'who will' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To push yourself beyond your strength is to strain by working too hard.

clue.text: Set out work to preclude using a legal term

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of set are put out of order

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A lawyer sets out a document to prevent some action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET into EST. OP is short for opus, a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: In law this verb means to bar someone from asserting something contrary to what they said before.

clue.text: At home, start to clean one's gold tooth

parts.note: someone at home is in

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so take the opening letter of clean

parts.note: one's read as 'one is' gives I and IS
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Back home, someone begins polishing a gold tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' stands for 'one is': I (one) plus IS. OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the sharp front biting teeth, a specific kind of tooth.

clue.text: Butt in with expletive, dismissing one cricket side

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the one and cricket side letters are removed

parts.note: an exclamation such as 'damn' is an interjection
I is the Roman numeral one
on, the leg side, is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: Someone interrupts with a curse after one side is dismissed at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' takes I and ON (one side of a cricket field, also called leg side) off the end of INTERJECTION. 'dismissing' suits cricket, where batters are dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrupt is to throw in a remark while someone else is speaking.

clue.text: Inedible bit of vegetable found in car

definitions.meaning: the hairy centre of a globe artichoke, which is thrown away
the valve on an older car engine that controls air intake for cold starts

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the fibrous heart of an artichoke and the starting control in an old motor.

clue.text: Any nice requests played for this anniversary?

indicators.note: requests played at a celebration are songs performed, and played also signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A radio station plays listeners' requests to celebrate an anniversary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges all fifteen letters of 'Any nice requests'.
explanation.definitionFit: This celebration marks one hundred and fifty years.

clue.text: Entitlement of king — Stephen?

definitions.meaning: the rights and prerogative belonging to a sovereign
King Stephen, the twelfth-century English monarch, was a member of the crown's ranks

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sovereign's prerogative and also kings and queens collectively, King Stephen being one; it also hints at an author's payment, as earned by Stephen King.

clue.text: Using "stealth"? Us pilot has it on manoeuvres in southern county

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the county name

parts.note: Surrey is a county in southern England, just south of London

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move about, so the letters of us pilot and it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pilot flying a stealth aircraft on exercises over a southern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on manoeuvres' rearranges USPILOTIT into PTITIOUSL, which 'in' places inside SURREY (an English county south of London) after SURRE. 'has' only joins the two fodder pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting by stealth means doing something secretly so as not to be noticed, which is acting furtively.

clue.text: Blue river follows a double bend

indicators.note: the river comes after the other pieces

parts.note: the letter Z has the shape of a double bend, as on road signs
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A river snaking through a double bend, its water blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Z is drawn like a double bend (the road sign for one shows a zigzag). URE is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bright sky-blue shade, a poetic word for the colour.

clue.text: Finally keep monarch up late, working non-stop

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of keep

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

indicators.note: something working is in action or being worked over, so the letters of up late are rearranged

explanation.surface: A courtier must keep the king up late, working without a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges UPLATE into PETUAL. ER is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never ceases is continuous, going on without any interruption.

clue.text: Taste, before importing one new fruit

parts.note: a tang is a sharp taste

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Tasting before bringing in a new kind of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like a link telling you to put TANG first, but it is the word ERE, which 'importing' fills with I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loose-skinned orange citrus is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Being popular, once led revolution, a result of laziness

parts.note: something popular is in

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters of once led are rearranged

explanation.surface: A popular leader of a revolution grows idle once in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' rearranges ONCELED into DOLENCE. 'Being' and 'a result of' only link the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness, an unwillingness to work, is the state of being lazy.

clue.text: Sickening type of shirt?

definitions.meaning: in British slang feeling poorly or unsteady, as in a weak heart

explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means unwell or shaky, and it also names a separate starched front worn under a dress jacket.

clue.text: Australian supporting evolutionary theory?

definitions.meaning: a native of Darwin, capital of Australia's Northern Territory
following Charles Darwin's theory of natural selection

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both someone from the Northern Territory capital and a believer in natural selection.

clue.text: Cover of everly brothers' song, perhaps, about the fifth

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the song word goes round the fifth

parts.note: the Everly Brothers sang as a pair, so any of their songs is an example of a two-voice piece
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A band records a cover version of an Everly Brothers number featuring a fifth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests a cover version of a song, but it is the bedcover. 'perhaps' marks the Everly Brothers' song as an example of a DUET; V is Roman five.
explanation.definitionFit: A continental quilt serves as the cover on a bed.

clue.text: Female I'd taken up to meet employees

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means read from the bottom, so I'd is reversed

parts.note: I'd gives the letters I and D
the staff are the employees

explanation.surface: A woman picked up by me to meet the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns ID into DI. 'to meet' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning staff was women's work, so the word describes the maternal side of a family.

clue.text: Having lost a seat, act to secure north, possibly

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the act word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a deed is an act

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of north may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A politician who lost a seat might act to win back the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges NORTH into THRON, which 'secure' puts inside DEED: DE-THRON-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch removed from power has been deposed, losing the throne they sat on.

clue.text: This solution will do!

parts.note: read as 'this answer will go down', since it is entered in a down light; do also means suffice

explanation.surface: Someone settling for an answer that is good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: To go down is exactly what an entry in a down column does.

clue.text: Tease American for rejecting choice sweet

indicators.note: rejecting suggests throwing back, so the tease and American words together are read backwards

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them
a plum job is a choice one

explanation.surface: An American teased for turning down a choice sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns RAG+US round as a whole to give SUGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small round boiled confection, the kind of candy of fairy-tale fame.

clue.text: We know them from long experience

definitions.text: We know them from long experience

parts.words: We know them from long experience
parts.note: the idiom of knowing how things work, from the cords sailors had to learn

explanation.surface: Old hands boasting of their familiarity with something.
explanation.definitionFit: To know the cords is an idiom for being familiar with how something is done, from sailing ships' rigging.

clue.text: Dressing for bed?

parts.note: not nightwear but a covering spread over a flower bed

explanation.surface: Getting ready for bed at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners spread compost or bark as a top layer over soil in a flower bed.

clue.text: Thoughts of some insipid easterner

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wondering what a dull person from the East might be thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Notions and concepts are what thinking produces.

clue.text: In the running, with two to go?

definitions.text: In the running, with two to go?

parts.words: In the running, with two to go
parts.note: a runner placed with two others still behind in the order, or a position counted back three from the end

explanation.surface: A competitor still in contention with two laps or rounds left.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means third from last: in a sequence, two more items follow it.

clue.text: Expect charge for carrying minerals

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the charge word goes around the minerals

parts.note: a fee is a charge
ores are minerals mined for metal

explanation.surface: Anticipating a fee for transporting minerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate something is to predict it before it happens.

clue.text: Sweet Japanese car, almost eye-catching

indicators.note: catching means trapping inside, so the shortened car holds the eye
almost means not quite all, so the car name loses its last letter

parts.note: Honda is a Japanese car maker
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sweet-looking Japanese car that nearly catches the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims HONDA to HOND, and 'catching' puts EYE inside it: HON-EYE-D.
explanation.definitionFit: Words described this way are sugary and flattering, as if coated in what bees make.
